tier_rationale: WiFIRE connectivity and a Traeger account exist, but the manufacturer's own product page states the grill's D2 Controller runs full temperature control and cooking on its own dial and display, and lists WiFIRE's contribution as remote monitoring, remote temperature adjustment and app recipes -- features layered on top of, not required for, a cook. Traeger's own burn-in guide confirms this directly rather than by inference: the entire first-use procedure for a WiFIRE grill is given as controller actions, with connecting the app appearing afterwards as a separate prompt. A Traeger account is created only inside the app during Wi-Fi pairing, which is a step you can decline and still cook. Vendor cloud exists, setup completes without it, core function is unaffected: D2.
the_unplug_test: Fill the hopper, flip the power switch, and turn the dial to a temperature: the auger primes, the igniter fires, and the D2 controller holds temperature and runs the full cook cycle exactly as it would connected, because none of that logic lives in the app. If the home network or Traeger's servers are down mid-cook, the grill keeps cooking; only the app's remote view goes dark. What Wi-Fi and an account add is monitoring and adjusting the cook from another room or away from home, in-app recipes and guided cook programs, and push alerts when the cook finishes.
offline_losses: remote monitoring and remote temperature adjustment from outside Bluetooth/Wi-Fi range
in-app recipes and Traeger's guided step-by-step cook programs
push notifications and cook-complete alerts routed through the app

repairability.notes: Traeger sells replacement D2/WiFIRE controllers, meat probes, augers and hopper parts directly through its parts store.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: 'D2 Controller' provides precise temperature maintenance as the grill's own control system; WiFIRE Technology is described separately as letting the owner 'monitor your cooks, adjust grill temperature, and access over 1,600 recipes through the Traeger App'; price listed at $799.99. No statement requires WiFi or an account for the grill to ignite or cook.

Third-party troubleshooting guide states that during a Traeger server outage 'your grill still works normally — you just cannot control or monitor it from the app,' and that the physical controller is used to cook as usual. Corroborating rather than load-bearing: consistent with the manufacturer's own D2-controller/WiFIRE split described in the primary source above, but not itself sufficient to carry the tier alone.

Traeger's own burn-in and seasoning guide gives the full first-use procedure for its WiFIRE grills (it names Ironwood, Timberline and Silverton) entirely as controller actions: power switch on, 'Press the power button on your controller to wake your controller screen', navigate to Select Auger > Prime Auger, set 350F and ignite, then 450-500F, then hold the controller power button to shut down. Connecting to the app appears afterwards as a separate prompt, not a step. Establishes that Traeger documents first use and cooking on the grill's own controller with the app as an optional layer -- the fact the D2 call rests on.

open_questions: Whether firmware updates pushed to the WiFIRE controller can be declined was not established.

FCC lookup for the specific WiFIRE/D2 controller module was not performed directly (only the grantee-level sibling check for traeger-tailgater-20); the manufacturer's own explicit description of WiFIRE as a Wi-Fi feature was treated as sufficient primary evidence of the radio's presence.
Current US price may vary; $799.99 was the manufacturer list price observed on the date above.
Whether the WiFIRE controller has any documented local API (e.g. LAN-only polling) independent of Traeger's cloud was not found; filed as local_api unknown rather than assumed absent.

Traeger's burn-in guide names Ironwood, Timberline and Silverton in its WiFIRE section rather than the Pro 575 specifically. The Pro 575 is a WiFIRE grill on the same D2 Controller, so the procedure applies, but a Pro-575-specific setup document would close the gap.
notes: Published as the D2 half of a same-brand pair with traeger-tailgater-20 (D0): same manufacturer and product category, same core mechanism, differing only in which controller module is fitted and what it's allowed to talk to. Filed under 'smoker' rather than 'grill' to give this pair coverage of both empty tools subcategories the brief flagged, since Traeger markets this whole line as a 'wood pellet grill and smoker' and the split is largely a taxonomy convenience rather than a functional distinction between the two Traeger SKUs.
local_replacement_note: No self-hosted replacement for the WiFIRE app/cloud was identified in this pass; the grill's own D2 controller already provides full standalone operation, so there was less pressure to find one.
